title: Tenant reservation realignment and soft-burst attenuation orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After the 2026-02-27 dedicated-cluster capacity spike, several tenant workloads experienced sustained tail latency and evictions. This ticket implements a coordinated set of follow-up items: a reservation re-alignment pass using temporal smoothing heuristics, a soft-burst attenuation orchestrator to avoid runaway token buckets, and a noisy-tenant isolation mode that incurs minimal cold-starts. Goal: reduce eviction rate by 90% for impacted clusters, bring 95th percentile latency under SLA, and avoid customer-visible retries during rollout.
root_cause_summary: The event was caused by (1) abrupt changes in per-request token distributions from a small number of tenants leading to KV-cache churn and eviction cascades; (2) aggressive reservation decay logic that under-allocated capacity during the burst tail; (3) burst tokenbucket settings allowed long-duration high-throughput sequences that starved co-located tenants. The autoscaler also misinterpreted short-lived spikes as sustained demand because of insufficient temporal smoothing of allocation metrics.
timeline: 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC: Traffic spike detected in cluster d-34; 3 tenants showed 10-20x increase in long-sequence requests.
2026-02-27 03:30 UTC: Eviction storm begins; several dedicated pods evicted leading to cascade and higher queue latency.
2026-02-27 04:05 UTC: Fallback to smaller model variants triggered; some endpoints returned degraded throughput.
2026-02-27 05:20 UTC: Incident declared; mitigation: rate-limited noisy tenants and temporary reservation bump for affected clusters.
2026-03-01 10:00 UTC: Postmortem draft published; initial action items triaged.
2026-03-05 09:00 UTC: ENG-209501 created to implement orchestration and permanent fixes.
2026-03-10 16:00 UTC: Spike-simulator PR reviewed and merged (see prs).
action_items: (A1) Implement reservation re-alignment service that re-evaluates tenant reservations every 10m using an EWMA of peak-quantiles (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 5).
(A2) Add temporal smoothing window to autoscaler to prevent reacting to sub-5m spikes; default window=15m configurable per pool (owner: Priya Desai, estimate: 3).

(A3) Introduce soft-burst attenuation: when a tenant exceeds 'burst-duration' threshold, reduce token-generation rate by 50% with exponential backoff instead of immediate hard throttle (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 5).

(A4) Noisy-tenant isolation mode: lightweight cgroup-like fencing that can be enabled per-tenant for 1h during investigation; fencing isolates KV-cache and metrics to prevent cross-tenant degradation (owner: Diego Ramirez, estimate: 8).
(A5) Create tenant synthetic workload tests and include them in the dedicated-cluster CI job to validate eviction surface under mixed workloads (owner: SRE team, estimate: 3).

(A6) Dashboard and alerting: add new alerts for (a) cross-tenant KV cache churn rate, (b) token-bucket saturation >80% for >5m, and (c) reservation decay delta >30% in 10m (owner: Observability, estimate: 2).
(A7) Run a staged rollout (canary 5% clusters, then 25%, then 100%) for the orchestration changes with rollback hooks and telemetries (owner: Release Eng, estimate: 2).
(A8) Post-release runbook update and customer communication template for 'transient capacity events' (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 1).
acceptance_criteria: Eviction rate for previously impacted tenants drops >=90% over a 7-day window after rollout.
95th percentile tail latency for dedicated clusters returns to SLA baseline within 24 hours of canary promotion to 25%.
Canary rollout exposes no increase in P0 incidents; automatic rollback triggers successfully on threshold breach.
CI synthetic test covers at least three mixed-workload scenarios (long-sequence-heavy tenant + many short requests + KV-warmup pattern).
notes: Trade-offs: soft-burst attenuation prefers graceful degradation over strict fairness; this reduces tail latency impact but allows noisy tenants to make progress with reduced rate.
Decision log: we rejected a hard-eviction-first strategy because it causes cascading cold-starts and customer-visible errors; chosen path emphasizes isolation + smoothing.
Review feedback: Security requested an audit of isolation mode interactions with KMS when fencing is active (assigned to Security team).
Follow ups: Evaluate whether per-tenant RV (reservation velocity) trend is a better signal than raw peak for autoscaler in a separate spike-analysis spike (see dependencies).
